_meta.purpose: Trigger evals for the SKILL.md description. A query passes when the skill is loaded exactly as should_trigger expects, measured as a trigger rate over N runs.
_meta.split_policy: Fixed at 12 train / 8 validation (60/40). Never optimize against the validation set — it exists only to detect overfitting. Keep the split stable across iterations so runs are comparable.

how_to_read_failures.should_trigger_false: Description too narrow, or the phrasing a developer would actually use is missing. Broaden toward the intent (implement / verify / diagnose), not the keyword.
how_to_read_failures.should_trigger_low_rate: Nondeterminism. Re-run before editing the description.
how_to_read_failures.should_not_trigger_true: Description too broad. This skill builds and verifies technical SEO; it should not load for keyword research, backlink analysis, content writing, or analytics reporting.

known_risks: The installed SEO family already covers research and content (seo-audit, seo-content, seo-plan, seo-backlinks). Negatives N2, N3, N7 police that boundary — those asks belong to those skills, not this one.
P4 and P9 name no framework, testing whether 'regardless of framework' phrasing is matched by intent rather than by framework keywords.
P7 and P8 describe symptoms with no SEO vocabulary at all. They test whether the description covers debugging, which is half the skill's job.
N5 is adjacent — generating hreflang tags is mechanical markup, not an implementation decision. It should not require this skill's playbooks.
N8 is infrastructure with no Search behaviour. It polices 'anything web-related' drift.

Deliberately NOT included as a negative: 'migrate our blog and keep the URLs'. That is redirect and site-move work, which this skill does cover, and marking it negative would train the description away from a real use case.
